name: Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain
clues: I was once the youngest Englishman to score in the Champions League.
I moved between two Premier League title rivals for thirty five million pounds.
I won a Premier League and a Champions League, as well as a Scottish league and cup double.
Knee injuries cost me a Euros and a World Cup, two years apart.
I grew up supporting Arsenal, played for them six years, and won my league titles elsewhere.
kickoff: I was born on the 15th of August 1993. I played 35 times for my country, scoring 7 goals.
story: Southampton's youngest ever first-team player, and for a while the most exciting teenager in England. The Ox cost Arsenal twelve million pounds at eighteen and spent seven years there collecting FA Cups and a reputation as a man who could play almost anywhere and settle nowhere. Liverpool made him a midfielder and he was flying when a knee gave way in a Champions League semi-final against Roma, costing him a year and a World Cup. He came back to win the title, and sat on the bench for the Champions League final he had helped them reach. His father played for England too. Thirty five caps, and then a late second act in Turkey and a league and cup double in Scotland, which is a better last chapter than the story looked like getting.
didYouKnow: He scored on his Champions League debut in 2011 and became the youngest Englishman to score in the competition, taking the record off Theo Walcott.
He returned from a severe knee injury exactly 366 days later, as a substitute against Huddersfield.
After changing his Liverpool shirt number he paid out of his own pocket to replace the shirts fans had already bought.

name: Angel Di Maria
clues: I scored in four different finals for my country, including the winner at an Olympics.
I was the most expensive signing a British club had ever made, and I left a year later for fifteen million less.
They call me Noodle, because of how thin I am.
I am the leading Argentine assist provider in Champions League history.
I wore the number seven at Manchester United for one season and it did not go well.
kickoff: I was born on the 14th of February 1988. I played 145 times for my country, scoring 31 goals.
story: Man of the match in a Champions League final, and then the most expensive flop in British football. Di Maria left Real Madrid for Manchester United for a British record fee, lasted one season, and was gone to Paris. What makes him remarkable is what came after: he scored the winner in a Copa America final, scored in a Finalissima at Wembley, and scored in a World Cup final. Argentina spent a decade being told he was finished and he kept turning up in the games that mattered most. Over a hundred and forty caps and more than twenty goals. He went home to Rosario Central at the end, where he started.
didYouKnow: Manchester United signed him in 2014 for what was then a British record fee of almost sixty million pounds.
He scored in the 2021 Copa America final, the 2022 Finalissima and the 2022 World Cup final.
They call him Fideo, which means noodle, because of how slight he is.

name: Antonio Valencia
clues: I topped the public vote for best young player at a World Cup and the award went to Lukas Podolski.
I held the record for Premier League appearances by a South American.
I lost a Champions League final at Wembley to Barcelona.
I took the number seven after Cantona, Beckham and Ronaldo, then asked to give it back.
I went from Wigan to Manchester United and stayed ten years.
kickoff: I was born on the 4th of August 1985. I played 99 times for my country, scoring 11 goals.
story: Ecuador's finest export, and the only man brave enough to take the number seven shirt after Cristiano Ronaldo. Valencia came from Wigan, where he had been the best winger in the league that nobody talked about, and the shirt crushed him for a season. He handed it back, took twenty five, and became indispensable. Then Jose Mourinho turned him into a right-back and he was arguably better again, winning Manchester United's players' player award and eventually the club captaincy. Two Premier League titles, a Europa League, ninety nine caps and a World Cup for Ecuador. He finished back at Quito, where nobody needs telling who he is.
didYouKnow: He grew up in poverty in Lago Agrio, helping his mother sell drinks outside the local stadium.
He left home at sixteen for El Nacional without telling his father, on a bus fare his brother paid for.
Alex Ferguson gave him the Manchester United number seven shirt in 2012, and he handed it back after one season.

name: Chris Smalling
clues: My manager publicly called me stupid for getting sent off in a derby.
I won the first ever Europa Conference League and was man of the match in the final.
I won two Premier League titles and later played in Saudi Arabia and Portugal.
I am a centre back who played under Jose Mourinho at two different clubs.
I came through at Millwall and grew up supporting Arsenal.
kickoff: I was born on the 22nd of November 1989. I played 31 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
story: Non-league to Old Trafford in two years. Smalling was playing for Maidstone United while studying at university when Fulham spotted him, and barely a season later Manchester United paid seven million pounds for a defender with twelve top-flight appearances. Two Premier League titles followed, and so did the criticism, including a manager telling the press in public that he and his partner were not brave enough. Rome fixed all that. He went to Roma on loan, stayed five years, won a European trophy under Jose Mourinho and was adored in a way he never quite was in England. Thirty one caps. Vegan, and happy to talk about it.
didYouKnow: He was a schoolboy national judo champion and came second in an international competition.
He was the first player in Premier League history to score two first half goals as a substitute.
He was man of the match in the 2022 Europa Conference League final, which Roma won as the inaugural winners.

name: Christian Benteke
clues: I scored the fastest goal in World Cup history, qualifying included, after eight seconds.
I won the MLS Golden Boot with twenty three goals.
I scored twice at Anfield, and two and a half years later I signed for them.
My family fled a dictatorship when I was small and I grew up in Belgium.
I cost Liverpool thirty two and a half million and they sold me to Crystal Palace a year later.
kickoff: I was born on the 3rd of December 1990. I played 45 times for my country, scoring 18 goals.
story: Six foot three of Belgian nuisance, and briefly the most talked-about striker in England. Benteke arrived at Aston Villa and dragged a sinking club to safety almost on his own, which earned him a thirty two and a half million pound move to Liverpool. There he scored an overhead kick against Manchester United that was better than anything else in his season, and left after a year anyway. Crystal Palace got the long tail of his career, then Washington, where he won the MLS Golden Boot at thirty three. More than sixty caps for a golden generation, usually as the option they turned to when the clever football ran out.
didYouKnow: He scored the fastest goal in any World Cup match, qualifying included, after 8.1 seconds against Gibraltar in 2016.
He ruptured his Achilles in training in April 2014 and missed the World Cup as Belgium's expected first choice striker.
He won the MLS Golden Boot with D.C. United in 2024, scoring twenty three goals.

name: Christian Vieri
clues: I won the trophy for the worst player in Serie A, and I had once been the most expensive footballer in the world.
I played for Juventus, Inter and AC Milan.
I won a Golden Boot in Spain and a Golden Boot in Italy, and only ever one league title.
I grew up in Sydney and I was better at cricket than football as a boy.
They called me Bobo, and I started a fashion label with Paolo Maldini.
kickoff: I was born on the 12th of July 1973. I played 49 times for my country, scoring 23 goals.
story: A club collector with a goal in him. Bobo Vieri played for both Milan clubs, both Turin clubs, Lazio, Atletico Madrid, Monaco and Fiorentina, among others, and never settled anywhere because somebody always paid more. Lazio sold him to Inter for a world record fee. He was the top scorer at the 1998 World Cup, got twenty three goals in forty nine games for Italy, and won precisely one Serie A title in all of it. Italy also voted him the biggest waste of talent in the league one year, which tells you how high the expectations were. Nine goals in nine World Cup matches. Nobody ever doubted the ability.
didYouKnow: He grew up in Sydney after his footballer father moved to Australia, and played youth football there.
Inter Milan signed him from Lazio in 1999 for what was then a world record fee.
He won the Golden Boot in Spain with Atletico Madrid and the Capocannoniere in Italy with Inter.

name: Conor Coady
clues: I was the first player from my club to start for England since 1990.
I played centre-back, and I captained England's under-twenties at a World Cup.
England's assistant manager called me the player of the tournament at a Euros where I never got on the pitch.
I came through at Liverpool and played twice for them.
I now coach the England under twenty ones.
kickoff: I was born on the 25th of February 1993. I played 10 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
story: The quietest two-tournament career England has produced. Coady went to a European Championship and a World Cup and did not play a minute of either, yet an England assistant called him the player of the tournament at the first one, for everything he did around the squad. He was the first Wolves player to start for England since Steve Bull in 1990, and he was so reliable that a run of eighty four consecutive Premier League games ended only because of a Covid contact. Two Championship titles, won at two different clubs. He was also named Football Ally of the Year at the British LGBT Awards. He coaches England's under twenty ones now.
didYouKnow: He played every minute of eighty four consecutive Premier League games for Wolves, a run of 7,560 minutes.
He was the first Wolves player to start for England since Steve Bull in 1990.
He was named Football Ally of the Year at the British LGBT Awards in 2021.

name: Daniel Sturridge
clues: I am the first Englishman to win the Champions League with two different English clubs.
Steven Gerrard's slip arguably cost me a league title.
I scored the winner against Wales at a European Championship.
I formed a fearsome front three with Suarez and Sterling.
I finished up at Trabzonspor and Perth Glory, and I am on Sky Sports now.
kickoff: I was born on the 1st of September 1989. I played 26 times for my country, scoring 8 goals.
story: The best strike partnership of the decade, and a career that could not hold itself together. Sturridge came through Manchester City, failed to break through at Chelsea, and then found Luis Suarez at Liverpool and scored twenty one league goals in a title race they lost by two points. He got England's winner against Wales at a European Championship. He also got a worldwide ban for breaching betting rules over information about his own transfer, which he always insisted was a conversation with family. Twenty six caps, a Champions League winner's medal from the bench, and the nagging sense of a player whose body never gave him a clear run.
didYouKnow: He scored eight goals in twelve appearances during a half season loan at Bolton Wanderers in 2011.
He was the first Englishman to win the Champions League with two different English clubs.
He ended his playing career in Australia with Perth Glory and has been a Sky Sports pundit since 2023.

name: Danny Welbeck
clues: I made my England debut against the country my parents came from.
I am still playing in the Premier League, at one of the biggest clubs in the country.
I won an FA Cup at a London club and missed the final injured.
United let me go the same week they signed Falcao.
I am Brighton's all-time leading Premier League scorer.
kickoff: I was born on the 26th of November 1990. I played 42 times for my country, scoring 16 goals.
story: Manchester United sold him and he scored the winner that knocked them out of the FA Cup. Welbeck came through at Old Trafford, won two league titles, and was moved on to Arsenal at twenty three for a fee that looked small even then. He gave Arsenal a Champions League hat-trick against Galatasaray, an FA Cup, and two serious injuries including an ankle that bent the wrong way at the Emirates. England kept picking him because the ball kept going in: sixteen goals in forty two caps, better than reputations suggest. Watford, then Brighton, where he was still scoring in the Premier League past thirty three.
didYouKnow: He scored a Champions League hat-trick for Arsenal against Galatasaray in 2014, the first treble of his career.
He scored the goal that knocked his former club Manchester United out of the FA Cup at Old Trafford in 2015.
He became Brighton's all time leading Premier League scorer before joining Chelsea in 2026.

name: Dennis Bergkamp
clues: I was named after a Scottish striker, and my parents had to add a letter to the spelling to get it past the registrar.
An Italian newspaper renamed its donkey of the week award after me.
Bobby Robson said after one of my goals that you just had to accept I had done a beautiful thing.
I am the only Dutchman in the English Football Hall of Fame.
I was Arsenal's record signing in 1995 and I stayed eleven years.
kickoff: I was born on the 10th of May 1969. I played 79 times for my country, scoring 37 goals.
story: The non-flying Dutchman, who would not board a plane and still became the most elegant footballer in England. Bergkamp's time at Inter was miserable and his time at Arsenal was transformative: he was the first foreign star to say yes to the club, and he arrived at a place that then won three titles and a Cup Winners' Cup, and went a whole league season unbeaten with him in the side. He once took all three places in Match of the Day's goal of the month, which no one else has done. There is a statue of him outside the Emirates and a place in the Premier League Hall of Fame. The touch, people still say, was the best there has been.
didYouKnow: His father named him after Denis Law, with an extra letter added because the registrar rejected the original spelling.
His fear of flying earned him the nickname the Non-Flying Dutchman.
His goal against Newcastle in 2002 was voted the best goal of the Premier League's first twenty five years.

name: Dida
clues: I saved three penalties in a European Cup final.
I am a World Cup winner who did not play a minute of the tournament.
I was the first Brazilian goalkeeper nominated for the Ballon d'Or, and I finished second in the world goalkeeper vote in 2005.
Andriy Shevchenko said I was the first man he embraced after scoring his penalty against Buffon.
I played volleyball before football, and I helped break a prejudice about black goalkeepers in Brazil.
kickoff: I was born on the 7th of October 1973. I played 91 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
story: Three saved penalties in a Champions League final shootout. Dida was AC Milan's goalkeeper across the great Ancelotti era and won two European Cups, the first on a night in Manchester where he was simply unbeatable from twelve yards. He was in Brazil's squad when they won the World Cup, without playing a minute of it. He is remembered in Britain for something else entirely: a Celtic supporter ran on and brushed past him, and he went down as though shot, which earned him a ban and a lot of jokes. Ninety one caps. Still one of the most decorated goalkeepers of the century.
didYouKnow: He saved three penalties in the 2003 Champions League final shootout against Juventus.
He is the only player to appear in five Confederations Cups, and leads the competition for appearances and clean sheets.
In 2006 he became the first black goalkeeper in fifty six years to start a World Cup match for Brazil.

name: Diego Costa
clues: I scored seven goals in my first four Premier League games, which nobody had managed before.
I have two caps for the country I was born in and twenty four for the one I chose.
I won the Premier League twice and La Liga twice.
A French newspaper named me the most hated footballer in the world.
I was named after an Argentine, my brother was named after a Brazilian, and I ended up playing for Spain.
kickoff: I was born on the 7th of October 1988. I played 24 times for my country, scoring 10 goals.
story: Born in Brazil, capped by Brazil, and then a Spain international. Costa made the switch after two friendlies and spent the rest of his career being the most disagreeable man on any pitch he stood on, in the way his managers loved and everyone else resented. He won a La Liga title with Atletico Madrid, two Premier Leagues with Chelsea, and found out he was being sold by text message. He went back to Atletico and won the league again. There was also a short, strange spell at Wolves at the end. Twenty four goals in Spain's shirt, and roughly the same number of enemies.
didYouKnow: His father named him after Diego Maradona, despite the rivalry between Brazil and Argentina.
He played two friendlies for Brazil in 2013 before switching his international allegiance to Spain.
Antonio Conte told him by text message in 2017 that he was no longer in Chelsea's plans.

name: Diego Milito
clues: My brother played for Barcelona, and I scored four goals against Real Madrid in a single cup tie.
I scored both goals in a Champions League final and was named man of the match.
I had two separate spells at the same Italian club before the big move finally came.
I spent three years in Spain and won nothing, then won four trophies in a single season in Italy.
I am now the president of the Argentine club where I started and finished.
kickoff: I was born on the 12th of June 1979. I played 25 times for my country, scoring 4 goals.
story: They called him El Principe, and on one night in Madrid he played like one. Milito scored both goals in the 2010 Champions League final and was named man of the match, the centrepiece of a season that brought Inter four trophies. He had done something stranger four years earlier, putting four past Real Madrid in a single cup tie while playing for Zaragoza. Three years in Spain brought him nothing at all. He had two separate spells at Genoa before the big move came, won twenty five caps in total for a man with over two hundred club goals, and is now president of the Argentine club where he began and finished.
didYouKnow: He scored both goals in the 2010 Champions League final against Bayern Munich and was named man of the match.
He put four goals past Real Madrid in a Copa del Rey semi-final for Real Zaragoza in 2006.
He has been president of Racing Club, where he began and finished his career, since December 2024.

name: Dirk Kuyt
clues: I lost a World Cup final and a Champions League final.
I arrived in England as a striker and spent most of my time there on the right wing.
I scored all three goals in a win over Manchester United, playing for one of their biggest rivals.
Rafael Benitez said you could call me Mr Duracell, because I was always running and always on the go.
I won league titles in Turkey and in the Netherlands, and never one in England.
kickoff: I was born on the 22nd of July 1980. I played 104 times for my country, scoring 24 goals.
story: Not the quickest, not the most skilful, and somehow always exactly where the ball was. Kuyt scored a hat-trick against Manchester United for Liverpool in which all three goals travelled a combined few yards, which is the perfect summary of him. He played a Champions League final and a World Cup final and lost both. The Netherlands picked him a hundred and four times. The best bit came last: he went home to Feyenoord and won the league title in his final season, scoring a hat-trick on the final day to do it. One hundred per cent effort, every single week, for twenty years.
didYouKnow: He scored a hat-trick on the final day of 2016-17 to win Feyenoord their first title in eighteen years, then retired three days later.
He scored Liverpool's goal in the 2007 Champions League final, a 2-1 defeat to AC Milan.
He scored a hat-trick against Manchester United at Anfield in March 2011.

name: Duncan Ferguson
clues: I became the most expensive footballer in Britain and played fourteen league games for the club that bought me.
I share the Premier League record for red cards with Patrick Vieira and Richard Dunne.
Burglars picked my house twice, and both times one of them ended up in hospital.
I have scored more Premier League goals than any other Scot.
I scored a hat-trick of headers, and nobody had done that in the Premier League before.
kickoff: I was born on the 27th of December 1971. I played 7 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
story: A Scottish centre-forward who went to prison for something he did on a football pitch. Big Dunc headbutted an opponent while at Rangers and served three months, which is the most extreme item on a long list. He had two spells at Everton with a Newcastle detour in between, scored a famous amount with his head, and holds a share of the Premier League record for red cards. He fell out with Scotland and ended with only seven caps. Goodison adored him anyway, because he once chased two burglars out of his own house and because he always, always ran at people. He later managed the club he loved, twice, as caretaker.
didYouKnow: He served a prison sentence in 1995 over an on-field headbutt on the Raith Rovers defender John McStay.
He shares the record for the most red cards in Premier League history with eight.
He was the first player to score a Premier League hat-trick entirely with headers.

name: Emmanuel Eboue
clues: I was booed by my own supporters while I was playing for them, and I came off in tears.
Sven named me in a World Cup squad, but not an England one.
I played more than two hundred games for Arsenal.
I started a Champions League final in Paris and lost it.
I am the Ivorian right-back from the Arsenal side that lost the 2006 Champions League final.
kickoff: I was born on the 4th of June 1983. I played 79 times for my country, scoring 3 goals.
story: Booed by his own supporters, and then applauded by them for years afterwards. Eboue had an afternoon at the Emirates where every touch was jeered, and the manager took him off to protect him. He came back from it and won two FA Cups, played in a Champions League final, and was one of the most popular players in the dressing room. Ivory Coast's golden generation used him as a right-back and sometimes a winger, and he won over a hundred caps. The hardest part came later: a Turkish title at Galatasaray, then a ban, a divorce and a public account of losing everything that he told with remarkable honesty.
numbers: 3 goals in 79 caps for Ivory Coast
didYouKnow: He started for Arsenal in the 2006 Champions League final at the Stade de France.
A section of Arsenal's own supporters booed him during a home match against Wigan in December 2008.
He signed for Sunderland in 2016 but a one year ban meant he never played a competitive minute for them.

name: Emmanuel Petit
clues: I scored in a World Cup final, and it was the thousandth goal in my federation's history.
I appeared as myself in a Christmas episode of The Bill.
The same manager signed me twice, nine years apart, at two different clubs.
I won the Double in my first season in England, and later lost an FA Cup final to that same club.
I played in Arsenal's midfield alongside Patrick Vieira, and later in Chelsea's alongside Frank Lampard.
kickoff: I was born on the 22nd of September 1970. I played 63 times for my country, scoring 6 goals.
story: A blond midfielder who scored the goal that ended a World Cup final. Petit's ball into the net at the Stade de France made it three nil, and he and Patrick Vieira went back to Arsenal having won the whole thing a few weeks after winning a Premier League and FA Cup double together. Add a European Championship two years later and he had, briefly, won everything worth winning. Barcelona took him for a single poor season, Chelsea got the rest. He grew up at Monaco. His career had the shape of an arrow: Highbury for the glory, and the summer of 1998 above everything.
didYouKnow: He scored France's third goal in the final minute of the 1998 World Cup final against Brazil.
He wore the number seventeen throughout his club career in tribute to his brother Olivier, who died at that age.
Arsene Wenger signed him twice, first for Monaco as a teenager and then for Arsenal nine years later.

name: Fabian Delph
clues: I was Aston Villa's player of the year two seasons running, and that is the biggest award I ever won.
I won the Premier League twice, playing in a new position.
I played for England in the 2018 World Cup.
I ended my career at Everton.
I was a Leeds academy midfielder who ended up playing left-back for Pep Guardiola.
kickoff: I was born on the 21st of November 1989. I played 20 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
story: He told the cameras he was not going anywhere, and was a Manchester City player within the week. Delph was Aston Villa's captain and best midfielder, and the move made him a figure of fun before it made him a champion twice over. He had the better of the deal: two Premier League titles, and a season where Pep Guardiola turned him into a left-back and it worked. England took him to a World Cup semi-final, and sent him home mid-tournament for the birth of his daughter before he flew straight back out. Twenty caps, a long injury list, and a knack for being useful in whatever role was going.
didYouKnow: He captained Aston Villa in the 2015 FA Cup final, which they lost four nil to Arsenal.
He said publicly he would stay and captain Aston Villa, then signed for Manchester City six days later.
An injury to Benjamin Mendy turned him into Manchester City's first choice left-back during their record breaking 2017-18 season.

name: Fabio Quagliarella
clues: I equalled a scoring record that Gabriel Batistuta had set back in 1994.
I played my whole career in Italy, for eight different clubs.
I captained Sampdoria and finished my career there.
I won three league titles in a row without ever really being first choice.
I left my hometown club for their biggest rivals, and it took seven years for anyone to find out why.
kickoff: I was born on the 31st of January 1983. I played 28 times for my country, scoring 9 goals.
story: Serie A's top scorer at thirty six years old. Quagliarella scored in eleven consecutive league games that season, equalling a record held by Gabriel Batistuta, and won the Golden Boot about fifteen years later than anyone expected him to. The reason his career wandered through Udinese, Napoli, Juventus, Torino and Sampdoria is darker than restlessness: a stalker spent years sending threats to him and his family, and he left his hometown club without ever being able to explain why. The truth came out long afterwards and the apologies arrived with it. Twenty eight caps for Italy, and a late flowering that nobody begrudged him.
didYouKnow: He was Serie A's top scorer in 2018-19 with twenty six goals, at the age of thirty six.
He equalled Gabriel Batistuta's record by scoring in eleven consecutive Serie A matches.
He left his home city club Napoli after he and his family were threatened by a stalker over five years.

name: Fabrizio Ravanelli
clues: I won league titles with two different Italian clubs and never a trophy in England, France or Scotland.
I scored a hat-trick on my Premier League debut, finished the season with thirty one goals in all competitions, and we were relegated.
I was the best paid player in the league and I would not stop complaining about the training ground.
I scored in a European Cup final and three months later I was playing in the north east of England.
They called me the White Feather, because my hair went white young.
kickoff: I was born on the 11th of December 1968. I played 22 times for my country, scoring 8 goals.
story: The White Feather, named for the silver hair, who scored in a Champions League final and then signed for Middlesbrough. Ravanelli won the European Cup with Juventus in 1996 and three months later was in the north east of England, where he announced himself with a hat-trick against Liverpool on his debut. That season Boro reached two cup finals, lost both, and were relegated, which may be the most Middlesbrough sequence ever recorded. He went on to Marseille, Lazio and Derby. Twenty two caps for Italy. Always complaining, always scoring, and always with the shirt pulled over his face.
didYouKnow: His prematurely white hair earned him the nickname the White Feather.
He scored in the 1996 Champions League final and three months later was playing in the north east of England.
He scored a hat-trick on his Premier League debut for Middlesbrough against Liverpool.

name: Frederic Kanoute
clues: I won two UEFA Cups back to back and never won a league title anywhere.
I was born in France, played for France's under twenty ones, and ended up playing for Mali.
I scored on my Tottenham debut, nine minutes after coming on for Bobby Zamora.
I played for West Ham and Tottenham before I became a star in Spain.
I am the six foot four striker who is still Sevilla's highest scoring foreigner.
kickoff: I was born on the 2nd of September 1977. I played 38 times for my country, scoring 23 goals.
story: African Footballer of the Year, and the first winner born in Europe. Kanoute was French, chose Mali, and became the best thing to happen to Sevilla in a generation, winning two UEFA Cups and scoring against everybody. Before that he had been a West Ham and Tottenham striker who looked too languid to be as good as he was. He is remembered as much for his convictions: he covered up a betting company's logo on his shirt because his faith forbade it, and he paid for a mosque in Seville out of his own pocket when it was about to close. Thirty nine caps, and a presence larger than the statistics.
didYouKnow: Born in France, he was the first player born outside Africa to be named African Footballer of the Year.
He put more than seven hundred thousand dollars of his own money into buying a mosque in Seville.
He refused to wear Sevilla's gambling sponsor on religious grounds, so the club made him a brand free shirt.

name: Gabriel Agbonlahor
clues: I scored a hat-trick with my head, my right foot and my left foot, all inside seven minutes.
I never moved for a transfer fee in my entire career.
I was given the captaincy after Stiliyan Petrov's leukaemia diagnosis, and I later resigned it after being photographed with a shisha pipe.
I turned down a Nigeria call-up, was named in a provisional Nigeria squad anyway, and I could have played for Scotland too.
I am the Birmingham born striker who gave Aston Villa his whole career and won nothing.
kickoff: I was born on the 13th of October 1986. I played 3 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
story: One club, one city, and absolutely nothing to show for it. Agbonlahor came through Aston Villa's academy and stayed almost four hundred games, finishing as their all-time leading Premier League scorer, and in all that time he won not a single trophy. He lost a League Cup final and an FA Cup final instead. He was quick in a way that Premier League defences had no answer to in the late 2000s, got three England caps during the Capello years and then was never seen again. He captained the club, got relegated with it, and retired at thirty. Villa fans still argue about whether he was underrated or whether he stopped trying. Probably both.
didYouKnow: He spent his entire professional career at Aston Villa, the club he joined as a schoolboy in Birmingham.
He never moved for a transfer fee at any point in his career.
He was Aston Villa's record Premier League goalscorer until Ollie Watkins overtook him in May 2025.

name: Gonzalo Higuain
clues: I was born in France, I do not speak French, and I had to apply for the nationality of the country I played for.
The same manager had me at Napoli, Juventus and Chelsea.
I was only the third Argentine to score a World Cup hat-trick, after Batistuta and one man in 1930.
My only English trophy was a Europa League, won on loan.
I won three La Liga titles and three Serie A titles and never a single trophy with my country.
kickoff: I was born on the 10th of December 1987. I played 75 times for my country, scoring 31 goals.
story: Three finals in three summers, and a nation that never forgave him. Higuain was a genuinely outstanding striker, the man who scored thirty six goals in a single Serie A season for Napoli to break a record that had stood since the 1920s, and the man Juventus then paid a vast fee to take off them. For Argentina he scored the quarter-final winner that took them to a World Cup final, and the missed chances in the finals that followed are what people remember. He was born in France because his father was playing there. Five La Liga titles and three Serie A titles, and a career defined by three afternoons.
didYouKnow: He was born in Brest because his father was playing in France, and he only took Argentine citizenship in 2007.
He scored thirty six goals for Napoli in 2015-16, still the record for a single Serie A season.
Juventus paid Napoli ninety million euros for him, then the largest fee an Italian club had ever paid.

name: Guti
clues: I joined my club's academy at ten years old and left twenty four years later.
I won five league titles in Spain.
My no-look backheel set up Karim Benzema at Deportivo.
The blond hair and the temper were as famous as the passing.
I played in the Galactico era at Real Madrid.
kickoff: I was born on the 31st of October 1976. I played 13 times for my country, scoring 3 goals.
story: Real Madrid for seventeen years, and the most beautiful pass of the century. Guti came through the academy as a striker, became a midfielder, and spent his career as the Galactico who was not quite a Galactico, in and out of the side while collecting five league titles and three European Cups. The pass everyone remembers is a no-look backheel through a defence to set up Karim Benzema, which looks impossible every time you watch it. Spain gave him only thirteen caps, partly because of the temperament, partly because of the era. He finished at Besiktas and has coached since. Maddening, lazy, and occasionally the best footballer alive.
didYouKnow: He joined Real Madrid's academy at ten years old and left twenty four years later.
He began as a striker before his manager converted him into a playmaker.
He won three European Cups and never played a minute at a World Cup or a European Championship.

name: Helder Postiga
clues: Glenn Hoddle signed me and called me a young player of proven ability.
I played at two World Cups and three European Championships for Portugal.
I chipped my penalty straight down the middle in a shootout against England.
I spent a season flopping at Tottenham and then knocked England out at that summer's Euros.
I am the Portuguese striker who won two league titles at Porto.
kickoff: I was born on the 2nd of August 1982. I played 71 times for my country, scoring 27 goals.
story: Written off in England, and then he scored against England. Postiga was a Tottenham signing who managed one league goal in a season and was sent home to Porto as a failure, and within weeks he chipped a quarter-final equaliser past David James at a European Championship and ran to the camera. He had the career Spurs never saw: Porto, Sporting, Panathinaikos, Zaragoza, Valencia and Lazio, and twenty seven goals in seventy one games for Portugal. He played in two World Cups and three European Championships, and reached a final. In England he is a punchline. In Portugal he is a man who kept turning up when it counted.
didYouKnow: Tottenham paid Porto over six million pounds for him in 2003 and he scored one league goal before being sold back.
He equalised against England in the Euro 2004 quarter-final and then converted a Panenka in the shootout.
He ended his career in India, winning the 2016 Indian Super League with Atletico de Kolkata.

name: Hernan Crespo
clues: I was once the most expensive player in the world, and I never won a league title at that club.
I was signed by an Italian giant as a replacement for the Brazilian Ronaldo.
I played for both Milan clubs, and for Inter twice.
I scored thirty five goals for Argentina.
Claudio Ranieri signed me and Jose Mourinho loaned me out within a year.
kickoff: I was born on the 5th of July 1975. I played 64 times for my country, scoring 35 goals.
story: He scored in a Champions League final for a club that did not own him. Crespo was on loan at AC Milan from Chelsea on the night in Istanbul, and his backheel flick made it three nil at half time, which remains one of the loveliest goals ever scored in a final nobody won. His career was a procession of enormous fees: a world record for a defender's wage bill when Lazio bought him from Parma, then Inter, then Chelsea twice with two Italian loans in between. Serie A's top scorer in 2001, thirty five goals in sixty four games for Argentina, and he is a coach now. Elegant and ruthless at once.
didYouKnow: Lazio broke the world transfer record to sign him from Parma in 2000.
He scored twice for AC Milan in the 2005 Champions League final and still finished on the losing side.
He was the first player to score Champions League goals for five different clubs.

name: Hulk
clues: I won titles in Portugal, Russia, China and Brazil and never in a big five league.
I never played in England, and my Brazil debut was against them.
I spent three years in Japan, two of them in the second division, before anyone in Europe noticed.
My free kick won my club a Russian league title.
My father named me after a television series, because I was so strongly built.
kickoff: I was born on the 25th of July 1986. I played 49 times for my country, scoring 11 goals.
story: Named after a television programme by his own father, because of how strongly built he was. Hulk's career is the great argument for looking outside the obvious leagues: he won titles in Portugal, Russia, China and Brazil, and never played a minute in any of Europe's big five. Before any of that he spent three years in Japan, two of them in the second division, which is where he learned to hit a ball with that absurd left foot. A free kick of his won Zenit a Russian title. He played for Brazil, made his debut against England, and never played a club game in England. Sheer, unreasonable power.
didYouKnow: His nickname came from his father, a fan of the Incredible Hulk television series.
He scored thirty seven goals in forty two games on loan at Tokyo Verdy in Japan's second tier.
He has won league titles in Portugal, Russia, China and Brazil but never in a big five European league.

name: Ian Wright
clues: I was the country's leading scorer one season and still did not make the squad for that summer's tournament.
I released a single co-written with one of the Pet Shop Boys.
I lost an FA Cup final in a replay with one London club, then won two with another.
I broke my club's all-time scoring record, and Thierry Henry took it off me eight years later.
I scored a hundred and twenty eight league goals for Arsenal, and then spent years on Match of the Day.
kickoff: I was born on the 3rd of November 1963. I played 33 times for my country, scoring 9 goals.
story: Non-league at twenty one, and Arsenal's record goalscorer by thirty four. Wright was rejected as a kid, worked on building sites, and was playing Sunday football for Greenwich Borough when Crystal Palace took a chance on him. He came off the bench in an FA Cup final and scored twice. Then Arsenal, where he won a Golden Boot, a league title and a hundred and eighty five goals, a record that stood until Thierry Henry passed it. Thirty three England caps and nine goals. He is a broadcaster now, and one of the best there has been, which is a second career almost as distinguished as the first.
honours: Football League Second Division play-offs (Crystal Palace, 1989)
didYouKnow: He was still playing non-league football for Greenwich Borough when Crystal Palace signed him at twenty one.
He came off the bench in the 1990 FA Cup final and scored twice against Manchester United.
He broke Cliff Bastin's Arsenal scoring record in 1997 and revealed a shirt reading Just Done It.

name: Ivan Toney
clues: I scored thirty one goals in a single Championship season, which nobody had managed before.
I turned down the chance to play for Jamaica.
I came on in extra time at a Euros for one reason, and I scored the penalty.
I left the Premier League for Saudi Arabia for a reported forty million pounds.
I scored sixty seven league goals for Brentford.
kickoff: I was born on the 16th of March 1996. I played 10 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
story: A penalty taker so reliable that people stopped watching the goalkeeper. Toney came up through Newcastle's youth system without ever really playing, scored thirty one in a Championship season for Brentford, and then became the Premier League striker nobody could keep quiet. Then came an eight month ban for hundreds of breaches of betting rules, some of them on his own matches. He came back and scored a penalty in his first game. Two England caps, a huge move to Saudi Arabia, and a career with a hole blown through the middle of it that he refilled almost immediately. Nerveless is the word.
didYouKnow: He scored thirty one goals in the 2020-21 Championship season, a record for the division.
He was banned from football for eight months in 2023 after 232 breaches of betting rules.
He was the youngest player ever to appear for Northampton Town, debuting at sixteen.

name: Jaap Stam
clues: I won three league titles in England and never one in Italy or with Ajax.
I lost a European Cup final in Istanbul.
I was the most expensive defender in the world, and I gave up money of my own to make the deal happen.
My manager sold me after my autobiography came out, and years later he admitted it was a mistake.
I was banned for five months for a steroid.
kickoff: I was born on the 17th of July 1972. I played 67 times for my country, scoring 3 goals.
story: Alex Ferguson's biggest regret, by his own admission. Stam was the best centre-half in Europe during Manchester United's treble season, immovable and quick with it, and then he wrote an autobiography, and a few months later he was sold to Lazio. Ferguson later said it was the worst decision he ever made. Stam went on to Milan and Ajax and kept being excellent, won sixty seven caps for the Netherlands, and played in a World Cup semi-final. He managed Reading to a play-off final afterwards. The strange thing is that he was never actually dropped for football reasons, not once.
didYouKnow: Manchester United paid PSV around ten and a half million pounds for him in 1998, then a world record for a defender.
He was sold to Lazio in 2001 shortly after the publication of his controversial autobiography.
He later managed Reading and took them to the Championship play-off final in 2017.

name: Jack Rodwell
clues: I modelled the Great Britain kit for an Olympics and then was not picked for the squad.
One local paper called me the worst signing in my club's history, and another one agreed.
I captained the A-League All Stars against Barcelona.
I was signed by Manchester City for twelve million.
I am now probably most famous for my portrayal on Sunderland 'Til I Die, where I look like a right tosser.
kickoff: I was born on the 11th of March 1991. I played 3 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
story: He modelled the Great Britain kit for an Olympics and then was not picked for the squad, which is a cruelly accurate summary. Rodwell was Everton's great hope, a centre-half who could play in midfield, and Manchester City paid twelve million for him on the strength of it. He played almost nothing. At Sunderland he became a byword for the worst kind of contract, one local paper calling him the worst signing in the club's history, and his portrayal in a documentary series did not help. Three England caps. He went to Australia and captained an All Stars team against Barcelona, which is a better ending than most people realise.
didYouKnow: He became Everton's youngest ever player in European competition, appearing against AZ Alkmaar at sixteen.
Manchester City paid Everton twelve million pounds for him in 2012, yet he made only sixteen league appearances in two seasons.
He finished his career in Australia, playing for both halves of the Sydney derby.

name: Jack Wilshere
clues: I scored my first goal for my club ten days after my debut, at sixteen.
My manager said I had Spanish technique and an English heart.
I won the BBC goal of the season twice in a row, which nobody had done since the Premier League began.
My only major trophies are two FA Cups, and I never won a league title.
I was my club's youngest ever league debutant, and I took the record off Cesc Fabregas.
kickoff: I was born on the 1st of January 1992. I played 34 times for my country, scoring 2 goals.
story: Arsenal versus Barcelona, 2011, and for ninety minutes he was the best midfielder on the pitch. Wilshere was nineteen. The problem was never the talent, it was the ankles and the shins, and he spent the next decade having the career taken away from him a few months at a time. He still managed two FA Cups, thirty four England caps and a goal against Slovenia that lifted a whole stadium, plus the team goal against Norwich he started and finished. West Ham and Bournemouth followed, then retirement at thirty. He coaches Arsenal's youngsters now, which is where he started.
didYouKnow: He became Arsenal's youngest ever league debutant at 16 years and 256 days, breaking Cesc Fabregas' record.
He won the BBC Goal of the Season award in two consecutive seasons, 2013-14 and 2014-15.
He finished his playing career in Denmark with AGF Aarhus before retiring at thirty.

name: James Ward-Prowse
clues: I was the first midfielder to play every single minute of two consecutive Premier League seasons.
I was born in Portsmouth to Portsmouth-supporting parents and joined Southampton at eight.
Pep Guardiola called me the best free-kick taker he had ever seen.
I have scored more away free kicks in the Premier League than David Beckham.
I do a golf swing when I score, and I have gone back to Southampton.
kickoff: I was born on the 1st of November 1994. I played 11 times for my country, scoring 2 goals.
story: The best set-piece taker England has produced since David Beckham, and the numbers say so. Ward-Prowse has scored more Premier League free kicks than anyone except Beckham, and he built an entire top-flight career on it while captaining Southampton through some grim seasons. He did it without ever winning a trophy, which is the price of loyalty at a club like that. England gave him eleven caps and no tournament. There is more to him than free kicks, including a remarkable record for never missing a game, but the free kicks are why anyone outside Hampshire knows his name. West Ham, then Nottingham Forest.
didYouKnow: He has scored more away free kicks in the Premier League than David Beckham.
He was the first midfielder to play every minute of two consecutive Premier League seasons.
Pep Guardiola called him the best free-kick taker he had ever seen.

name: Javier Saviola
clues: I was the youngest ever South American Footballer of the Year, and I beat a record of Maradona's to it.
I took Spanish citizenship so my club could get round the limit on foreign players.
I was the youngest man on Pele's list of the greatest living footballers.
I played for Barcelona and then for Real Madrid, and I only won a league title at one of them.
I had four managers in six years at Barcelona, and Louis van Gaal was one of them.
kickoff: I was born on the 11th of December 1981. I played 39 times for my country, scoring 11 goals.
story: El Conejo, the rabbit, and once the most exciting teenager in South America. Saviola was five foot six and electric, and Barcelona paid a fortune for him when he was nineteen, and then he spent six years mostly being loaned out and being almost good enough. He scored freely for River Plate before and for Benfica afterwards, which suggests the problem was Barcelona rather than him. Then he did something nobody does and joined Real Madrid, where he played even less. An Olympic gold medal, a World Youth Championship, and forty caps for Argentina. The potential was never fully cashed.
didYouKnow: Barcelona paid around fifteen million pounds to sign him from River Plate at nineteen.
He scored eleven goals in seven games as Argentina won the 2001 World Youth Championship, a tournament record.
He crossed one of football's great divides by joining Real Madrid after six years at Barcelona.

name: Jens Lehmann
clues: I was in a World Cup final squad and never got on the pitch, because the man ahead of me was the best in the world.
I was voted the best goalkeeper in Europe twice, nine years apart.
I went eight hundred and fifty three minutes without conceding in the Champions League, then got sent off in the final.
I went through a Premier League season without losing a game.
I am the German goalkeeper from Arsenal's Invincibles.
kickoff: I was born on the 10th of November 1969. I played 61 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
story: Every minute of an unbeaten league season, and then sent off in a European Cup final. Lehmann was Arsenal's goalkeeper through the Invincibles and a man of magnificent contradictions: eight hundred and fifty three consecutive Champions League minutes without conceding, and also the club record for red cards at Borussia Dortmund by any player, not just any keeper. He won league titles in three different countries. He saved two penalties in a World Cup shootout against Argentina using notes hidden in his sock. He sat on the bench for a World Cup final behind Oliver Kahn, and was twice voted the best goalkeeper in Europe. Never dull, never quiet.
didYouKnow: He played every match of Arsenal's unbeaten 2003-04 Premier League season.
He is the only goalkeeper ever sent off in a European Cup final, dismissed against Barcelona in 2006.
He saved two penalties in Germany's 2006 World Cup shootout against Argentina using notes hidden in his sock.

name: Jermaine Beckford
clues: I could have played for England, Jamaica or Grenada, and I chose Jamaica.
I scored the goal that knocked Manchester United out of the FA Cup in the third round, the earliest Alex Ferguson had ever gone out.
I played for Leeds, and years later went on loan to Huddersfield.
I scored against both Liverpool at Anfield and Chelsea at Goodison in my one Premier League season.
I am a television pundit now, and my brother won Wayne Rooney's Street Striker.
kickoff: I was born on the 9th of December 1983. I played 6 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
story: He scored the goal that knocked Manchester United out of the FA Cup in the third round, the earliest Alex Ferguson had ever gone out. Beckford was a Leeds player in the third tier at the time, which made it worse. He could have played for England, Jamaica or Grenada and chose Jamaica. His one Premier League season brought goals at Anfield and against Chelsea at Goodison, and after that he dropped back down the leagues and kept scoring. He is a pundit now. His brother won a television football competition, which is the kind of detail that makes a family story rather than a career.
didYouKnow: He scored the only goal as League One Leeds knocked Manchester United out of the FA Cup third round in 2010.
He scored a hat-trick in the 2015 League One play-off final at Wembley to win Preston promotion.
He worked as a windscreen fitter for the RAC while playing non-league football for Wealdstone.

name: Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink
clues: I started out as a goalkeeper and ended up winning two Golden Boots.
The manager who released me from Middlesbrough hired me as an England coach many years later.
I went from Leeds to Chelsea by way of Spain, for a club record fee.
I was born in Suriname, played for the Netherlands, and I went back to coach Suriname.
The manager who signed me at Atletico Madrid turned up as my Chelsea boss a few months after I got there.
kickoff: I was born on the 27th of March 1972. I played 23 times for my country, scoring 9 goals.
story: He hit a football harder than almost anyone, and he scored wherever he went. Hasselbaink won the Premier League Golden Boot at Leeds, left for Atletico Madrid and got relegated with them while being their top scorer, then came back and won another Golden Boot at Chelsea. He is one of very few men to have shared the award twice with different clubs. Born in Suriname, raised in the Netherlands, he played at a World Cup and a European Championship. Middlesbrough and Charlton came at the end. He has managed since, with mixed results, and remains a man whose shooting you simply do not forget.
didYouKnow: He was born in Paramaribo, Suriname, and moved to the Netherlands at the age of five.
He won the Premier League Golden Boot twice, shared with Leeds in 1999 and outright with Chelsea in 2001.
He started out playing in goal as a boy before moving to winger and then forward.

name: Joaquin
clues: I played twenty seasons in La Liga and never won it.
I scored the first hat-trick of my career at thirty eight, and it broke a record of Alfredo Di Stefano's.
I was the most expensive signing in Valencia's history when they bought me.
I share the record for the most La Liga appearances ever, with a goalkeeper.
I spent most of my career at Real Betis.
kickoff: I was born on the 21st of July 1981. I played 51 times for my country, scoring 4 goals.
story: One of the great one-club loves, interrupted by eleven years elsewhere. Joaquin came through at Real Betis, left for Valencia and Malaga and Fiorentina, and then came home and played until he was forty one, by which time he had made more Primera Division appearances than almost anyone in history. He scored a Copa del Rey winner, lifted the trophy as captain, and became the oldest player to score a La Liga hat-trick. Fifty one caps for Spain, two World Cups, and the misfortune of being a right winger in the exact years Spain had an embarrassment of them. Always smiling, always running.
didYouKnow: He is the oldest player ever to score a hat-trick in La Liga, aged 38, breaking a record held by Alfredo Di Stefano since 1964.
He equalled Andoni Zubizarreta's record of 622 appearances in the Spanish top division.
He won the Copa del Rey with Real Betis at forty, seventeen years after lifting the same trophy with them.

name: John Carew
clues: I was the first black player to represent my country.
I won La Liga in 2001-02, but not with Real Madrid or Barcelona.
I am the six foot five Norwegian striker of Valencia, Lyon and Aston Villa.
I was signed by Aston Villa in a straight swap with Milan Baros.
I am a six foot five striker.
kickoff: I was born on the 5th of September 1979. I played 91 times for my country, scoring 24 goals.
story: Six foot five, Norwegian, and the first black player ever to represent his country. Carew was a problem nobody solved twice the same way: he knocked Arsenal out of Europe on two separate occasions for Valencia, won a La Liga title in Spain, and arrived at Aston Villa in a straight swap for Milan Baros. He scored his penalty in the 2001 Champions League final shootout and still went home with nothing, the first of three finals he would lose. There is a second act too, stranger than the first. He acts now, and played a jungle warrior opposite Angelina Jolie. Ninety one caps, twenty four goals, and a career that was never once boring.
didYouKnow: He was the first black player to represent Norway at senior level.
He has acted since retiring, including a role in Maleficent: Mistress of Evil opposite Angelina Jolie.
He knocked Arsenal out of the Champions League twice while playing for Valencia.

name: John McGinn
clues: I was speared in the thigh by a training pole thrown by my own club captain, and I took the club to court.
I joke that nobody in football has a backside as big as mine.
I scored my country's only goal at a World Cup, and it was our first win there in thirty six years.
I captained my club to a European trophy, only the third man ever to do it there.
I currently play for Aston Villa.
kickoff: I was born on the 18th of October 1994. I played 92 times for my country, scoring 22 goals.
story: Scotland's midfield for a decade, and Aston Villa's engine for longer than anyone expected. McGinn came from Hibernian, where he had won a Scottish Cup that ended a hundred and fourteen year wait, for a fee that now looks absurd. At Villa he scored in a play-off final to get them promoted, then stayed to captain them back into the Champions League. Steven Gerrard said he was the best player he had seen in training since he stopped playing with the very best. More than ninety Scotland caps and over twenty goals, and a brother who also played professionally. Everything he does looks slightly too energetic.
didYouKnow: He scored in Aston Villa's 2019 Championship play-off final win over Derby at Wembley.
He captained Aston Villa to the Europa League title in 2026, only the third man to lead the club to a European trophy.
His older brothers Paul and Stephen were also professional footballers, and all three played for St Mirren and Hibernian.

name: John O'Shea
clues: I went in goal in a Premier League game and saved a shot from my own international teammate.
I have fourteen winners' medals and hardly any individual awards.
I have won the Premier League five times and have been relegated twice.
Roy Keane tore into me in an interview the club refused to broadcast.
I am an Irish defender.
kickoff: I was born on the 30th of April 1981. I played 118 times for my country, scoring 3 goals.
story: A full-back, a centre-half, a midfielder, and once a goalkeeper, all at Manchester United. O'Shea played thirteen years there and won five league titles, a Champions League and a Club World Cup while never being anybody's first choice in any single position, which is a remarkable trick. He scored a last-minute winner at Anfield. He kept goal in a Premier League match when both keepers were unavailable, and he kept a clean sheet in it. One hundred and eighteen caps for Ireland, then Sunderland and Reading. The nutmeg on Luis Figo is still the clip people send each other.
numbers: 3 goals in 118 caps for Republic of Ireland
didYouKnow: He went in goal for Manchester United in 2007 after Edwin van der Sar was injured and all three substitutes had been used.
He scored a stoppage time winner at Anfield in March 2007 that proved pivotal in United's title win.
He served as interim manager of the Republic of Ireland in 2024.

name: Juan Pablo Angel
clues: I arrived at River Plate billed as the next Hernan Crespo.
Bradley Wright-Phillips is the only man who has passed my goalscoring record in New York.
I was a club record signing for Aston Villa at nine and a half million pounds.
My surname means angel, and supporters used to wear wings for me.
I took a ninety per cent pay cut to go home, then won three league titles in a row.
kickoff: I was born on the 24th of October 1975. I played 33 times for my country, scoring 9 goals.
story: Aston Villa's best Colombian, and a man whose first season in England was almost unbearable. Angel arrived for a club record fee, his wife lost a baby, and he barely played. The second season he scored twenty three. He went on to be one of the most liked players in the club's modern history, and then did it all again in New York, where he was the first designated player signing that actually worked and scored freely in Major League Soccer. Thirty four caps for Colombia. River Plate before, Los Angeles and Atlanta after. Quiet, decent, and much better than the fee suggested.
didYouKnow: Aston Villa signed him in 2001 for a club record fee of around nine and a half million pounds.
He was the New York Red Bulls' all time leading scorer until Bradley Wright-Phillips passed his total.
He took a ninety per cent pay cut to return to Colombia and won three league titles in a row.

name: Juan Roman Riquelme
clues: I said people complain that I never smile, but I have never seen Zidane laugh either.
Louis van Gaal played me on the wing and mostly left me out.
I went back to Argentina for fifteen million dollars, the most an Argentine club had ever paid.
I was a Barcelona number ten who got loaned to a small Spanish club and was far better there.
Jens Lehmann saved a last minute penalty that would have taken a Champions League semi-final to extra time.
kickoff: I was born on the 24th of June 1978. I played 51 times for my country, scoring 17 goals.
story: The last of the true number tens, and he refused to be anything else. Riquelme would not run back, would not press, would not move out to the wing when Louis van Gaal asked him to at Barcelona, and so he barely played there. Everywhere he was allowed to stand still and receive the ball he was sublime: two Copa Libertadores and an Intercontinental Cup with Boca Juniors, and a Villarreal side he dragged to a Champions League semi-final before missing the penalty that would have taken them to the final. Olympic gold with Argentina, fifty one caps, and a reputation in Buenos Aires that borders on the religious.
didYouKnow: He was the eldest of eleven children in a poor family from San Fernando, Buenos Aires.
Louis van Gaal dismissed him at Barcelona as a political signing and he spent most of that contract on loan.
He has been president of Boca Juniors since 2023, the club where he was the defining player of its modern era.

name: Julio Cesar
clues: I have won a treble that included the Champions League.
I was man of the match in a World Cup last sixteen, and two games later we lost seven one.
I was one of four Champions League winners in a QPR squad that got relegated.
I dribbled out of my own box four nil down and my manager called me an idiot in public.
I am the Brazilian goalkeeper from Inter's treble who later turned up at QPR.
kickoff: I was born on the 3rd of September 1979. I played 87 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
story: For two or three years he was simply the best goalkeeper in the world. Julio Cesar was Inter's goalkeeper in the treble season, won a Champions League, and collected individual awards from everyone who hands them out. Brazil picked him eighty seven times. He saved two penalties in a World Cup shootout on home soil and wept openly about it, and a week later he was the goalkeeper in the seven one. In between he had a season at Queens Park Rangers that ended in relegation and which he always spoke about generously. Flamengo, Benfica, Toronto. One of football's genuinely well-liked men.
didYouKnow: He kept goal for Inter's 2010 treble side under Jose Mourinho.
He holds Brazil's record for the longest run without conceding, 581 minutes.
He was registered to Chievo purely to get round a Serie A quota and never played a game for them.

name: Juninho Pernambucano
clues: I beat Oliver Kahn from distance with a free kick, and that is the goal that made my name in Europe.
I won seven league titles in a row with a club that had never won one before I arrived.
I went to court to get out of my contract so I could leave Brazil.
I have scored more than seventy goals direct from free kicks, and plenty say nobody ever hit them better.
I am the Brazilian free-kick specialist of Lyon, and I later became their sporting director.
kickoff: I was born on the 30th of January 1975. I played 40 times for my country, scoring 6 goals.
story: The greatest free-kick taker who has ever lived, and it is not really a debate. Juninho scored around seventy five of them, from distances that should be impossible, with a technique he worked out himself by striking the ball on the valve. He won seven consecutive league titles at Lyon and is the club's record scorer from midfield. Brazil gave him only forty caps because the competition in that era was brutal, and he played at a World Cup. Vasco da Gama before and after. Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale both studied his technique. Nobody has ever matched it.
honours: Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A (Vasco da Gama, 1997)
Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A (Vasco da Gama, 2000)
didYouKnow: He scored more than seventy career goals direct from free kicks and is widely rated the finest free-kick taker the game has seen.
He developed the knuckleball free kick, struck with almost no spin so the ball moves unpredictably in flight.
He beat Oliver Kahn with a dipping long range free kick for Lyon against Bayern Munich.

name: Jussi Jaaskelainen
clues: I won fifty six caps and never played at a single tournament, because we never qualified.
I was bought for a hundred thousand pounds and played five hundred and thirty games for the club.
A double save of mine was voted third best in the Premier League's first twenty years.
I played most famously under Big Sam.
I bet you cannot spell my name.
kickoff: I was born on the 19th of April 1975. I played 56 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
story: Bolton Wanderers for fifteen years, more than five hundred games, and a hundred thousand pounds well spent. Jaaskelainen came from Vaasa in Finland for the kind of fee that would not buy a Premier League substitute now, and ended up as one of the best shot-stoppers in the division across an era when Bolton were in Europe and beating everybody. He saved two penalties in the same match against Blackburn, which is the clip Bolton fans still share. Then West Ham and Wigan. Fifty six caps for a Finland side that never qualified for anything, which is the only medal missing from a career of remarkable consistency.
didYouKnow: Bolton bought him from VPS for a hundred thousand pounds in 1997, after a trial at Norwich City.
He made 530 appearances for Bolton across fifteen seasons.
He won fifty six caps for Finland and never played at a major tournament, because they never qualified.

name: Kaka
clues: I nearly joined Manchester City for over a hundred million pounds, and fans gathered outside my house to stop me.
I am one of only a handful of men to win a World Cup, a European Cup and a Ballon d'Or.
I was the second biggest fee ever paid at the time I was transferred.
I was three nil up at half time in a European Cup final and lost it on penalties.
I am the Brazilian playmaker of Milan and Real Madrid, and I never played in the Premier League.
kickoff: I was born on the 22nd of April 1982. I played 92 times for my country, scoring 29 goals.
story: The last man to win the Ballon d'Or before Messi and Ronaldo took it over for a decade. Kaka's 2007 was close to perfect: he tore the Champions League apart almost single-handedly and Milan won it. He had been a World Cup winner at twenty, a squad player who barely featured, and he was in Brazil's team for years afterwards. A swimming pool accident as a teenager fractured a vertebra and nearly ended everything before it began, which he always described as the reason he played with the shirt reading that he belongs to Jesus. The Real Madrid move never worked. Ninety two caps, and universally liked.
didYouKnow: He fractured his spine in a swimming pool accident as a teenager and was warned he might never play again.
Real Madrid signed him from AC Milan in 2009 for around sixty seven million euros.
His nickname came from his younger brother, who could not pronounce Ricardo as a small child.

name: Kalvin Phillips
clues: I started every match of a European Championship, including a final we lost on penalties.
My manager apologised in public for calling me overweight.
I gave my first England shirt to Marcelo Bielsa.
I cost forty two million pounds and then went six hundred and forty five days between appearances for the club.
I was called the Yorkshire Pirlo.
kickoff: I was born on the 2nd of December 1995. I played 31 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
story: They called him the Yorkshire Pirlo, and Pirlo himself agreed, calling him a bit of a regista. Phillips came through at Leeds, the hometown boy in a side Bielsa dragged back to the top division, and he gave his first England shirt to the manager who made him. He started every match of a European Championship, including the final England lost on penalties, and was voted his country's player of the year. Then a forty two million pound move to Manchester City, and the harder half of the story: six hundred and forty five days between appearances, a manager apologising in public for calling him overweight, and a succession of loans. The talent was never the question.
didYouKnow: Leeds supporters nicknamed him the Yorkshire Pirlo for his passing range from deep.
Marcelo Bielsa converted him from a box to box midfielder into a specialist defensive midfielder.
He gave his first England shirt to Bielsa, the manager who had made him.

name: Kim Kallstrom
clues: I won two Ligue 1 titles with Lyon.
I played in five different countries.
I played three league games for an English club and came away with an FA Cup.
A back injury was found in my medical and the club signed me anyway, so I did my rehab on their time.
I am the Swedish midfielder who turned up at Arsenal on loan from Spartak Moscow.
kickoff: I was born on the 24th of August 1982. I played 131 times for my country, scoring 16 goals.
story: He arrived at Arsenal with a broken back, and left with an FA Cup. Kallstrom's loan from Spartak Moscow is one of the strangest in Premier League history: the medical found a fracture, Arsenal signed him anyway because they were desperate, and he played three league games in four months before collecting a winner's medal at Wembley. The rest of the career was substantial. Two Ligue 1 titles with Lyon, spells in five different countries, and a hundred and thirty one caps for Sweden, which puts him among their most capped players of all time. A beautiful striker of a ball when his spine allowed it.
didYouKnow: He arrived at Arsenal on loan in January 2014 with a cracked vertebra in his back and still won the FA Cup that season.
He converted a penalty in Arsenal's FA Cup semi-final shootout win over Wigan.
He is Sweden's fourth most capped player of all time.

name: Laurent Robert
clues: I equalled David Beckham's record for free-kick goals in a single Premier League season.
I won nine caps for France and not one of them came at a World Cup or a European Championship.
I was fined a hundred and eighty thousand pounds for criticising my manager in public, and that manager was Graeme Souness.
I played for Newcastle and then on loan at Portsmouth, and I never won a thing at club level.
I am the French left winger who gave Newcastle five years and hit free kicks for a living.
kickoff: I was born on the 21st of May 1975. I played 9 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
story: A left foot that could do absolutely anything, attached to a man who did not fancy defending. Robert was Newcastle's winger through the Bobby Robson years and hit some of the best goals the club has seen, from free kicks and from thirty yards, and he fell out spectacularly with Graeme Souness when Souness asked him to track back. He went to Portsmouth, Benfica and eventually Australia. France capped him nine times. He is the exact type of footballer the Premier League has largely stopped signing: thrilling, selfish, and worth the ticket on his own.
didYouKnow: He was the first player from the island of Reunion to represent France.
He scored five free-kick goals in the 2001-02 Premier League season, matching David Beckham's single season record.
Newcastle fined him around a hundred and eighty thousand pounds after he criticised Graeme Souness in the press.

name: Leon Britton
clues: I made a hundred and forty one Premier League appearances and never scored in any of them.
I won a League Cup at Wembley with a club that had been in the bottom division not long before.
I was five foot four, and in 2011 I was statistically the best passer in the world, ahead of Xavi.
They gave me the freedom of the city of Swansea.
Supporters passed buckets round the ground to pay for my loan, and they called it the Battle For Britton.
kickoff: I was born on the 16th of September 1982. I was never capped by my country.
story: Five foot four, and in 2011 statistically the best passer in the world, ahead of Xavi. Britton went to Swansea when they were in the bottom division and still there when they were beating Manchester United, which is as complete a club story as English football has produced. He made a hundred and forty one Premier League appearances and never scored once. He won a League Cup at Wembley. The supporters once passed buckets round the ground to raise the money for his loan fee and called it the Battle For Britton. They gave him the freedom of the city in the end, and nobody argued.
didYouKnow: West Ham paid Arsenal four hundred thousand pounds for him at sixteen, the highest fee ever paid for a player that age at the time.
Swansea supporters part funded his 2002 loan with a bucket collection they called the Battle For Britton.
In 2011 he was the most accurate passer in world football among players with over a thousand passes, ahead of Xavi.

name: Les Ferdinand
clues: I was a painter and decorator playing non-league when a London club took a chance on me.
My cousin captained England and won the Champions League.
I came off the bench in Alan Shearer's testimonial to a huge ovation, and then won the penalty he scored with the last kick of his career.
I was a record signing for Newcastle and scored twenty nine goals in my first season there.
I also played for Spurs, West Ham, Leicester, Bolton and Watford.
kickoff: I was born on the 8th of December 1966. I played 17 times for my country, scoring 5 goals.
story: Sir Les, from Hayes in the Isthmian League to the Premier League Player of the Year. Ferdinand was a late starter who got better the longer he went on: Queens Park Rangers made him, Newcastle made him famous during the Keegan years, and Tottenham got the elegant later period, including the ten thousandth goal in Premier League history. Seventeen England caps, and no tournament to show for them. He is a director of football at the club where he began now. There are three Ferdinands in the professional game and he was the first, which is worth remembering.
didYouKnow: He scored the ten thousandth goal in Premier League history, for Tottenham against Fulham in December 2001.
He is a second cousin of the football playing brothers Rio and Anton Ferdinand.
He was a painter and decorator playing non-league football for Hayes before QPR signed him.

name: Lomana LuaLua
clues: I scored against my own parent club while on loan, and the FA changed the rules because of it.
I played at four Africa Cup of Nations and captained my country, and I never played at a World Cup.
Bobby Robson signed me, then told the press I should keep my mouth shut and do what I was paid for.
I did seven back flips when I scored, and one of them injured me during a game against Arsenal.
My brother and two of my cousins all played professionally, and one of them is Yannick Bolasie.
kickoff: I was born on the 28th of December 1980. I played 31 times for my country, scoring 7 goals.
story: Seven back flips after every goal, and one of them injured him during a match against Arsenal. LuaLua was a Bobby Robson signing at Newcastle, where he was more entertainment than reliability, and the manager once told the press he should keep his mouth shut and do what he was paid for. He went to Portsmouth and then, on loan at Olympiacos, scored against Portsmouth, which was so obviously absurd that the rules were changed afterwards. Four Africa Cup of Nations and the captaincy of DR Congo, and never a World Cup. His brother and two of his cousins played professionally too, one of them Yannick Bolasie.
numbers: 7 goals in 31 caps for DR Congo
didYouKnow: He injured himself performing his trademark somersault celebration against Arsenal in 2006 and missed matches as a result.
His brother Kazenga and his cousins Yannick Bolasie and Tresor Kandol also became professional footballers.
He scored against his own parent club while on loan, and the FA changed the loan rules because of it.

name: Luis Garcia
clues: I scored the winner against Juventus and the winner against Chelsea on the way to a European Cup final.
I was on Barcelona's books for four years without playing a first-team game, and they later had to buy me back.
Jose Mourinho called one of my goals a ghost goal.
The crowd sang that I drank sangria and came from Barca to bring them joy.
I won the Champions League with Liverpool in 2005 and never won a thing in Spain.
kickoff: I was born on the 24th of June 1978. I played 18 times for my country, scoring 4 goals.
story: He scored in every round of a Champions League they had no business winning. Garcia's goal against Chelsea in the semi-final may or may not have crossed the line, and twenty years later Liverpool and Chelsea supporters still cannot agree, which is exactly the point. He was at Anfield for three years, came from Barcelona, went to Atletico Madrid afterwards, and in that short window produced the most important goals of anyone in a red shirt. Twenty caps for Spain. The song the Kop wrote about him is still sung by people who never saw him play, which is a kind of immortality.
didYouKnow: His disputed ghost goal against Chelsea sent Liverpool through to the 2005 Champions League final.
He scored a hat-trick against Slovakia in a World Cup qualifying play-off ahead of the 2006 tournament.
He was on Barcelona's books for four years without playing a first-team league game and they later bought him back.

name: Marcelo
clues: I won a Copa Libertadores back home after fifteen years in Spain.
I scored the opening goal of a World Cup in my own country, and it was an own goal.
Roberto Carlos says I am the best left back in Real Madrid's history.
I won five European Cups.
I was a left back who frankly could not defend.
kickoff: I was born on the 12th of May 1988. I played 58 times for my country, scoring 6 goals.
story: Twenty five trophies, more than any player in Real Madrid's history. Marcelo arrived at eighteen from Fluminense and stayed fifteen years, redefining what a left-back could be and winning five Champions Leagues, the last of them as club captain. He was never a defender in the conventional sense and it did not matter, because almost nobody got past him and because the attacking was worth any risk. Fifty eight caps for Brazil, two Olympic bronzes, and the misfortune of a generation that never won a World Cup. He went home to Fluminense at the end and won the Copa Libertadores there too.
didYouKnow: He overtook Paco Gento to become the most decorated player in Real Madrid's history.
He was the first foreign player to captain Real Madrid in more than a century.
He scored the opening goal of the 2014 World Cup in his own country, and it was an own goal.

name: Marco Materazzi
clues: I was sent off three times in a single season in England.
The most famous incidents involving me happened on a football pitch but had very little to do with the football being played.
I scored the equaliser in a World Cup final.
Zinedine Zidane said he would rather die than apologise to me.
I won the treble at Inter Milan.
kickoff: I was born on the 19th of August 1973. I played 41 times for my country, scoring 2 goals.
