story: He scored the equaliser in a World Cup final and then got headbutted in the chest in front of the world. Materazzi's 2006 is the most famous thing about him and it should not be: he also converted a penalty in the shootout that won it. He spent a decade at Inter, winning a Champions League and five league titles, and was a defender of the old Italian school, which is to say that he fouled people. There was one season at Everton early on, which nobody remembers and he did not enjoy. Forty one caps. Perugia and Lazio before, and a great deal of noise throughout.
didYouKnow: He conceded the penalty and then scored Italy's equaliser in the 2006 World Cup final, and was headbutted by Zinedine Zidane in extra time.
He scored twelve goals for Perugia in 2000-01, a Serie A record for a defender in one season.
He spent the 1998-99 season in the Premier League with Everton before returning to Italy.

name: Mark Noble
clues: I scored twenty eight Premier League penalties and missed only five.
I had Irish grandparents and I turned down the chance to play for Ireland, because I thought a kid who had dreamed of it deserved it more than me.
My club renamed their young player of the year award after me.
I had retired and taken a desk job at the club when Declan Rice walked a European trophy over and handed it to me to lift.
Sam Allardyce said I looked five foot eight but stood six foot four every time I pulled the shirt on.
kickoff: I was born on the 8th of May 1987. I was never capped by my country.
story: Seventeen years, five hundred and fifty appearances, one club, and not a single England cap. Noble was West Ham, in every sense: a local boy who captained them, got them promoted twice, and stayed through every version of the club including the move away from the ground he grew up next to. He was a proper midfielder, a reliable penalty taker, and the symbol of something the Premier League has almost run out of. The last act was a substitution brought on specifically to take a penalty against Manchester United, and he missed it, which somehow made everyone love him more. He is the sporting director now.
honours: Football League Championship play-offs (West Ham United, 2005)
Football League Championship play-offs (West Ham United, 2012)
didYouKnow: He was never capped by England at senior level, despite eighteen years as a professional and twenty under-21 appearances.
He made 550 appearances for West Ham United and was club captain for seven years.
He returned to West Ham as the club's sporting director in January 2023.

name: Nemanja Matic
clues: The same manager signed me at three different clubs.
Chelsea bought me for one and a half million, sold me as part of the deal for David Luiz, then paid fourteen times that to get me back.
I won two Premier League titles at Chelsea, but I made more Premier League appearances for another of the big clubs, only just.
I played youth football for both Red Star Belgrade and Partizan.
I scored Manchester United's goal of the season in 2017-18.
kickoff: I was born on the 1st of August 1988. I played 48 times for my country, scoring 2 goals.
story: Chelsea sold him, then bought him back for roughly ten times the money. Matic went to Benfica as part of a deal for David Luiz, became one of the best midfielders in Europe there, and Chelsea paid up to correct their own mistake. He won two Premier League titles with them and scored a volley in an FA Cup semi-final at Wembley that no defensive midfielder has any business hitting. Manchester United, Roma, Rennes and Lyon followed. He retired from international football early and still finished with close to fifty caps for Serbia. Enormous, calm, and almost impossible to hurry.
didYouKnow: He joined Benfica in 2011 as part of the deal that took David Luiz to Chelsea, and Chelsea bought him back three years later.
Benfica converted him from a playmaker into a defensive midfielder under Jorge Jesus.
His half volley against Crystal Palace in 2018 was voted Manchester United's goal of the season.

name: Nemanja Vidic
clues: I lost two Champions League finals and won one.
My transfer was agreed on Christmas Day and then I had to wait for a work permit.
I am the only defender to have been voted the Premier League's player of the season twice.
I won five league titles and three League Cups at one club, and never the FA Cup.
Robin van Persie said I put my head where other players were scared to put their feet.
kickoff: I was born on the 21st of October 1981. I played 56 times for my country, scoring 2 goals.
story: Half of the best central defensive partnership the Premier League has seen. Vidic came from Spartak Moscow in January, had a difficult first six months, and then spent eight years being the most uncompromising defender in England. Five league titles, a Champions League, and two Premier League Player of the Year awards, which almost no defender wins once. Serbia and Montenegro conceded one goal in their entire qualifying campaign for a World Cup with him in the side, and then he missed the tournament through injury and they were taken apart. Fifty six caps. Inter at the end. He simply did not go round people, and nobody went round him.
honours: First League of Serbia and Montenegro (Red Star Belgrade, 2004)
didYouKnow: Manchester United agreed to sign him on Christmas Day 2005 and he arrived once his work permit came through.
He is the only defender ever to win the Premier League Player of the Season award twice.
Robin van Persie said he put his head where other players were scared to put their feet.

name: Ngolo Kante
clues: Arsenal passed on me twice and signed Granit Xhaka instead.
I used to get to training on a kick scooter, and I have an accounting diploma.
I am the first outfield player since Eric Cantona to win back-to-back English titles with different clubs.
I turned down Mali twice and never played for France at any youth level.
They say seventy per cent of the planet is covered by water and the rest by me.
kickoff: I was born on the 29th of March 1991. I played 69 times for my country, scoring 2 goals.
story: He won the Premier League, and then he won it again with somebody else. Kante was playing in the French third tier not long before Leicester City signed him, and he was the engine of the strangest title win in history, then moved to Chelsea and won the thing again the very next season. Add a World Cup, a Champions League in which he was man of the match in the final, a Europa League and a PFA Player of the Year award, and the only sensible conclusion is that he is the most quietly decorated footballer of his generation. He is famously modest, famously small, and famously everywhere.
didYouKnow: He was born in Paris to Malian parents and turned down an approach from Mali before the 2015 Africa Cup of Nations.
He won back to back Premier League titles with two different clubs, Leicester and Chelsea.
He was made a Knight of the Legion of Honour in 2018 after France won the World Cup.

name: Nicky Butt
clues: I walked out on my manager after he picked his own son ahead of me.
I was player of the year at my second club, and I captained them to a Championship title.
I scored in Eric Cantona's comeback match.
I started a European Cup final only because our captain was suspended, and I played every minute of it.
I won six league titles and every one of them was at Manchester United.
kickoff: I was born on the 21st of January 1975. I played 39 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
story: The forgotten one of the Class of 92, and the one who started a European Cup final. Butt only played in Barcelona because Roy Keane was suspended, and he played every minute of it, which is a good enough career highlight for anybody. Six league titles, all at Manchester United, and a treble. He scored in Eric Cantona's comeback match. Afterwards he was player of the year at Newcastle and had spells at Birmingham and Hull, and he walked out on one manager over a selection he thought was indefensible. Thirty nine England caps, and not a goal in any of them.
didYouKnow: He came through Manchester United's academy as one of the Class of 92 alongside David Beckham and Paul Scholes.
He started the 1999 Champions League final because Roy Keane was suspended, and played every minute of it.
He finished his playing career in Hong Kong with South China.

name: Oliver Kahn
clues: I played for two clubs in my life and both were German.
I was voted Europe's best goalkeeper four years running.
I won the Champions League in 2000-01.
But I famously lost a Champions League final to a late comeback.
They called me the Titan, and I was in goal when England won five one in Munich.
kickoff: I was born on the 15th of June 1969. I played 86 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
story: The only goalkeeper ever to win the Golden Ball at a World Cup, and he spent the final itself making the mistake everyone remembers. Kahn was Der Titan, the most intimidating presence in the Bundesliga for a decade and a half, and he won eight league titles and a Champions League with Bayern Munich, saving three penalties in the shootout in the final. Before Bayern there was Karlsruher SC. Eighty six caps, and a rivalry with Jens Lehmann that defined German goalkeeping for years. He came back as the club's chief executive, where he discovered that the job is harder from a desk.
didYouKnow: He is the only goalkeeper ever to win the Golden Ball as the best player at a World Cup, taking it in 2002.
He saved three penalties in the shootout to win Bayern Munich the 2001 Champions League final against Valencia.
He was sent off in 2001 after going up for a corner and punching the ball into the net.

name: Oriol Romeu
clues: I have a Champions League medal and I never won a senior cap for Spain.
Pep Guardiola gave me my debut, and in that first spell I played one league game for them.
The only individual awards of my career all came in a single season at Southampton.
I won a La Liga title off one league appearance.
I am the Spanish defensive midfielder who ended up in Japan.
kickoff: I was born on the 24th of September 1991. I was never capped by my country.
story: A Barcelona boy who had to leave to have a career, and then got to go home. Romeu came through La Masia, could not get near the first team, and was sold to Chelsea at nineteen, where he was in the squad that won a Champions League. Southampton gave him six years and the holding role in front of the back four, where he was underrated to the point of invisibility. Then Girona played brilliantly with him in the side and Barcelona bought him back at thirty one, which almost never happens to anybody. Spain never capped him once. Not every good career needs an international record.
didYouKnow: He was never capped by the senior Spain side, playing only up to under twenty one level and four times for Catalonia.
He won a La Liga title off a single league appearance for Barcelona in 2010-11.
He won the Champions League and the FA Cup with Chelsea in his first season after leaving Barcelona.

name: Pablo Zabaleta
clues: I lost a World Cup final and a Copa America final, and won an Olympic gold.
I scored the first goal on the day my club won their first league title in forty four years.
I signed for my club one day before Abu Dhabi bought it.
I also played for West Ham.
I was a right back.
kickoff: I was born on the 16th of January 1985. I played 58 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
story: The warrior, and the most popular right-back Manchester City have had. Zabaleta arrived from Espanyol in the last hours of the window on the day the club was taken over, which means he saw the whole thing from the beginning: two Premier League titles, including the one decided in the final seconds of the final day, and nine years of running into people slightly harder than was necessary. Argentina picked him fifty eight times, won Olympic gold with him and lost a World Cup final with him. West Ham got the last two years. He never scored for his country, which nobody held against him.
didYouKnow: He scored the opening goal in the win over Queens Park Rangers that clinched Manchester City the 2012 title.
He signed for Manchester City one day before the club was bought by Abu Dhabi.
He was sent off in the 2013 FA Cup final, only the third player ever dismissed in one.

name: Pascal Gross
clues: I scored my club's first ever Premier League goal.
I assisted four goals in one Bundesliga match, only the third man ever to do it.
I was my club's all-time Premier League top scorer until Danny Welbeck passed me.
I won a Premier League player of the month at thirty five, and I am back at Brighton.
I did not play for my country until I was thirty two.
kickoff: I was born on the 15th of June 1991. I played 19 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
story: He scored Brighton's first ever Premier League goal, and then spent most of a decade being their best player. Gross came from Ingolstadt for a small fee and turned into the most intelligent attacking midfielder in the division that nobody outside the south coast discussed, which included a Premier League Player of the Month award in his mid thirties. He once assisted four goals in a single Bundesliga match, something only two men had managed before him. Germany did not cap him until he was thirty two, which is the most Pascal Gross fact imaginable. Nineteen caps, and a club record that took Danny Welbeck to beat.
didYouKnow: He scored Brighton's first ever Premier League goal, against West Bromwich Albion in September 2017.
He did not make his Germany debut until 2023, at the age of thirty two.
He wears long sleeved shirts because of a grass allergy.

name: Patrick Bamford
clues: I was offered a place at Harvard and a place in their football team, and I turned both down.
I was on Chelsea's books for five years, never played a game for them, and went out on loan seven times.
I went to a fee-paying school with no football team, so I played rugby at full-back until I was fifteen.
I scored my first career hat-trick against Leeds and signed for them four months later.
I scored seventeen Premier League goals in my first season with a newly promoted Leeds.
kickoff: I was born on the 5th of September 1993. I played 1 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
story: Seventeen Premier League goals in a season, and one England cap to show for everything. Bamford spent his early twenties on loan from Chelsea to half the Championship without ever playing a minute for them, was voted the best player in that division, and finally found a home at Leeds, where Marcelo Bielsa made him into a genuine top-flight centre-forward. He got promoted, had the best season of his life, and then injuries arrived and took the rest of it. He is one of the game's more thoughtful figures, outspoken on mental health and on the environment, and happy to say so when it would be easier not to.
didYouKnow: He turned down a place at Harvard University, and a place in their football team, to stay in English football.
He had seven separate loan spells during five years as a Chelsea player and never made a competitive appearance for them.
He scored seventeen Premier League goals for a newly promoted Leeds in 2020-21.

name: Patrick Kluivert
clues: I went out of three major tournaments in a row at the semi-final stage, and two of them went to penalties.
I held my country's goalscoring record until Robin van Persie passed me.
I spent six years at Barcelona and won one trophy.
I also played for Newcastle.
I was the six foot three Dutch striker who partnered Rivaldo at Barcelona.
kickoff: I was born on the 1st of July 1976. I played 79 times for my country, scoring 40 goals.
story: Eighteen years old, on as a substitute, and the winner in a European Cup final. Kluivert remains the youngest player ever to score in one, and that night with Ajax was the summit rather than the start of something. What followed was six years at Barcelona that produced exactly one trophy, a Dutch goalscoring record that stood until Robin van Persie passed it, and the cruellest pattern in international football: three major tournament semi-finals in a row, two of them lost on penalties. He also played for Newcastle, which fewer people remember. He has coached almost everywhere since, from Curacao to Barcelona's academy to Indonesia.
didYouKnow: He came off the bench at eighteen to score the winner in the 1995 Champions League final, and is still the youngest scorer in a final.
He scored a hat-trick in the 6-1 Euro 2000 quarter-final against Yugoslavia and shared the tournament's Golden Boot.
His forty goals were the Netherlands record until Robin van Persie passed him in 2013.

name: Per Mertesacker
clues: I won a World Cup and more than a hundred caps, and I never won a league title in any country.
I won three FA Cups with a London based Premier League club.
My nickname came from a Roald Dahl book, and I used it as the title of my autobiography.
I had three clubs in my whole career, and two of them were German.
I ran Arsenal's academy for eight years, and I am about to start a big job with the German federation.
kickoff: I was born on the 29th of September 1984. I played 104 times for my country, scoring 4 goals.
story: Six foot six, and sick with nerves before every single match. Mertesacker admitted long afterwards that he used to vomit before kick-off and spent his career dreading the thing he was best at, which makes a hundred and four caps and a World Cup winner's medal rather more impressive than they already were. At Arsenal he was the calmest man in a chaotic defence, and the story everyone tells is the FA Cup final he started having barely played all season, and won. He is the academy manager there now, which suits him exactly. The BFG, they called him, and he liked it.
didYouKnow: His blunt interview given from an ice bath at the 2014 World Cup became a viral sensation in Germany.
He captained Arsenal to victory in the 2017 FA Cup final having barely played all season through injury.
He took charge of Arsenal's academy immediately after retiring in 2018.

name: Peter Crouch
clues: I took the Premier League record for substitute appearances off Shola Ameobi, and James Milner later took it off me.
I was my country's top scorer in a qualifying campaign and we still did not make the tournament.
I played for both Portsmouth and Southampton, and I did Portsmouth twice.
I hold the Premier League record for headed goals.
I was famous for my celebration as much as my goals.
kickoff: I was born on the 30th of January 1981. I played 42 times for my country, scoring 22 goals.
story: Six foot seven, and a better footballer than the joke allowed. Crouch played for eleven clubs, scored a hundred Premier League goals, and was particularly good at the thing nobody expected of a man that height, which was controlling the ball on the floor. For England he got twenty two goals in forty two games, a ratio most strikers would take, and did the robot celebration at a World Cup. He is as famous now for the podcast and the self-deprecation as for the football, which is a little unfair, because he was an excellent player for a very long time. The line about what he would be without football is immortal.
didYouKnow: He holds the record for the most headed goals in Premier League history.
He marked goals with a deliberately stiff robot dance that he first unveiled before the 2006 World Cup.
He played for both Portsmouth and Southampton, and had two separate spells at Portsmouth.

name: Phil Jagielka
clues: I played a hundred and thirty three league games in a row, including every minute of one season.
Neil Warnock said I would be world class at tiddlywinks.
I was called into a Euros squad only because Gareth Barry got injured.
I captained Everton for six years and played more than eight hundred senior games.
I was Sheffield United's player of the season three years running.
kickoff: I was born on the 17th of August 1982. I played 40 times for my country, scoring 3 goals.
story: He once kept goal for Sheffield United in the Premier League era because he was the designated emergency goalkeeper, and he kept a clean sheet. Jagielka then became Everton's captain and one of the most reliable centre-halves in the country for a decade, got forty England caps, and scored a stoppage-time equaliser in a Merseyside derby at Anfield that is still the loudest thing most Evertonians have heard. He missed a penalty in a European Championship shootout. He won nothing at all, not one trophy in a twenty year career, which happens to good defenders at good-but-not-great clubs more often than anyone admits.
didYouKnow: He made his Sheffield United debut while still a trainee and was given a professional contract the next day.
He played 133 consecutive league games for Sheffield United, including every minute of the 2006-07 season.
He was the first Everton player ever to captain England, and became their most capped England international.

name: Phil Neville
clues: I scored in the shoot-out that knocked my old club out of an FA Cup semi-final.
I captained England at cricket as a boy, and I was the youngest player ever to turn out for Lancashire's second eleven.
I was naturally right footed and spent years filling in at left-back.
I won six league titles at one club and nothing at all in eight years at the next.
My brother and I were the first siblings ever to captain opposing Premier League sides.
kickoff: I was born on the 21st of January 1977. I played 59 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
story: Six league titles, fifty nine England caps, and zero goals for his country. Neville was the squad man who was somehow never quite a squad man, playing full-back on either side and in midfield for Manchester United across a decade of trophies, then captaining Everton for years afterwards. The one moment that followed him around was a penalty conceded against Romania that sent England out of a European Championship. He coached, then managed England's women to a World Cup semi-final, then went to Miami. His brother and his sister were both internationals too, in two different sports, which is an unusual family.
didYouKnow: He captained England Under-15s at cricket and is the youngest player ever to appear for Lancashire's second eleven.
He and his brother Gary were the first siblings to captain opposing Premier League sides.
He managed England's women's team to fourth place at the 2019 World Cup.

name: Raul
clues: I scored at the Camp Nou and put my finger to my lips.
I was runner up for the Ballon d'Or in 2001.
I fell out with my national manager over squad rules and never played for my country again, which was poorly timed, because they won the next three major tournaments without me.
I won the Champions League three times.
Fernando Hierro called me the Ferrari, and I kissed my wedding ring when I scored.
kickoff: I was born on the 27th of June 1977. I played 102 times for my country, scoring 44 goals.
story: Real Madrid's record goalscorer for most of the modern era, and a man Atletico let slip across the city. Raul was in Atletico's academy when they shut it down, so he walked into Real Madrid instead and scored three hundred and twenty three goals for them, a record that only Cristiano Ronaldo has beaten. Six league titles and three Champions Leagues. For Spain he has a hundred and two caps and forty four goals, and not one trophy, because he belonged to the generation immediately before the good one and retired from international football just too early. Schalke and New York afterwards. He manages now.
didYouKnow: He came through Atletico Madrid's youth system and only joined Real Madrid because Atletico's president shut the academy to save money.
He made 741 appearances for Real Madrid, a club record, scoring 323 goals.
He was never sent off in his entire professional career.

name: Raul Meireles
clues: I was suspended for a Champions League final and still got a medal.
I played for Liverpool and then for Chelsea, one season each.
The same manager had me at Porto and at Chelsea.
I joked that I won the ink championship against Agger and Skrtel.
I went to two World Cups and two Euros for Portugal, and I retired just before they won one.
kickoff: I was born on the 17th of March 1983. I played 76 times for my country, scoring 10 goals.
story: The mohawk, the tattoos, and a trophy collection that is quietly ridiculous. Meireles won a league title and a European trophy with Porto, moved to Liverpool and was voted their player of the year within a single season, then went to Chelsea and won a Champions League and a Europa League in two years. Add a Portuguese cup haul and a Turkish title at Fenerbahce and he has won more than most of the famous names of his era. Portugal capped him seventy six times and he reached a European Championship semi-final. He looked like a man in a band and ran like a man with a deadline.
didYouKnow: He won the Champions League with Chelsea in 2012 despite being suspended for the final.
He was voted the PFA Fans' Player of the Year during his single season at Liverpool.
He played at two World Cups and two European Championships for Portugal.

name: Ricardo Quaresma
clues: I was given an award for being the worst player in the league, and the next season my club won the treble.
I inherited Luis Figo's number seven shirt.
My trademark was a bending shot with the outside of my right foot, and it has its own name.
Jose Mourinho said at Inter Milan that I had great talent but still had to learn to work for the team.
I scored a 117th minute winner in a knockout tie at a European Championship, in a tournament we would go on to win.
kickoff: I was born on the 26th of September 1983. I played 80 times for my country, scoring 10 goals.
story: Nobody has ever hit a ball quite like it. The trivela, struck with the outside of the right foot and bending away from the goalkeeper, was Quaresma's signature and his argument: that there is more than one way to play. Italy gave him an award for being the worst player in the league, and the following season his club won the treble. Jose Mourinho said he had the talent but still had to learn to work for the team. He inherited Luis Figo's number seven anyway. He sat through an entire European Championship without kicking a ball, then came back four years later and scored a hundred and seventeenth minute winner on the way to Portugal lifting the thing. Maddening, magnificent, entirely himself.
didYouKnow: He is famous for the trivela, a curling shot struck with the outside of his right foot.
He scored the extra time winner against Croatia at Euro 2016 and the decisive penalty in the quarter-final shootout against Poland.
He waited fifteen years after his first cap to appear at a World Cup, finally playing in 2018.

name: Robbie Fowler
clues: I won young player of the year twice running and never once won the senior player of the year award.
I told the referee I had not been fouled, took the penalty anyway, missed it, and won a fair play award for it.
I once held the record for the fastest hat-trick in Premier League history, and it stood for twenty years.
My club fined me sixty thousand pounds for a celebration, and my manager told the press I had been eating grass.
I am in the top ten scorers in Premier League history and I never won a league title.
kickoff: I was born on the 9th of April 1975. I played 26 times for my country, scoring 7 goals.
story: They called him God on Merseyside, which tells you everything. Fowler scored a hundred and eighty three goals for Liverpool, including a hat-trick in four and a half minutes that stood as the fastest in Premier League history for over twenty years, and he was part of the treble side in 2001. England gave him only twenty six caps because Shearer, Sheringham and then Owen were in the way. Leeds, Manchester City and a brief emotional return to Anfield followed. He invested the money so well in property that his name became slang for being unexpectedly rich, which he has always found funny.
didYouKnow: He scored a hat-trick against Arsenal in 1994 in four minutes and thirty three seconds, a record that stood for twenty years.
Liverpool supporters nicknamed him God during his peak years at Anfield.
He told a referee he had not been fouled, took the penalty anyway, missed it, and won a fair play award for it.

name: Robert Pires
clues: I was signed for six million pounds, replacing a winger who had left for Barcelona.
I scored eight times against Tottenham, and at their ground in five straight seasons.
I was taken off after eighteen minutes of a Champions League final because our goalkeeper was sent off, and it was my last game for the club.
I set up the golden goal that won a European Championship final.
I tried to pass a penalty to Thierry Henry, failed to make proper contact, and it went down as my miss.
kickoff: I was born on the 29th of October 1973. I played 79 times for my country, scoring 14 goals.
story: The best left foot in the Premier League for about four years, and a World Cup winner before he arrived. Pires came from Marseille with a France medal already in the bag and took a season to adjust, after which he was voted Footballer of the Year, won two league titles and three FA Cups, and was central to a side that went a whole season unbeaten. Seventy nine caps and a European Championship too. Villarreal got the late years and he turned up at Aston Villa at thirty six for a handful of games. He also took part in the most embarrassing penalty in Arsenal's history, which he has lived down.
didYouKnow: He came through the Metz academy and made his senior debut for them in 1993 against Lyon.
He scored against Tottenham on eight separate occasions during his Arsenal career.
He was made a Knight of the Legion of Honour in 1998 after France won the World Cup.

name: Roy Makaay
clues: They called me Das Phantom, because I appeared out of nowhere.
I won the Golden Shoe for Deportivo La Coruna.
I scored a hat-trick against a German giant in the Champions League, and they then signed me for a club record fee.
I was kept out of my national side by Kluivert, Bergkamp and van Nistelrooy.
I was later a coach at Rangers.
kickoff: I was born on the 9th of March 1975. I played 43 times for my country, scoring 6 goals.
story: They called him Das Phantom because he appeared out of nowhere, and the clock agreed: ten and a bit seconds into a Champions League tie at Real Madrid, he had scored the fastest goal in the competition's history. Makaay won the European Golden Shoe at Deportivo La Coruna and remains their leading scorer of all time. He announced himself to Bayern Munich by putting a hat-trick past them, and they responded by paying a club record fee to make him theirs. For the Netherlands he was unlucky rather than unwanted, kept out by Kluivert, Bergkamp and van Nistelrooy, and he never played at a World Cup. He coaches now, including a spell at Rangers.
didYouKnow: He scored the fastest goal in Champions League history against Real Madrid in 2007, timed at 10.12 seconds.
He is still Deportivo La Coruna's all time leading scorer.
He scored a hat-trick on his Deportivo debut and another in the last professional match he ever played.

name: Santi Cazorla
clues: I was uncapped when they picked me for a European Championship, and we won it.
I took free kicks with either foot, and the stats had my shots almost exactly fifty fifty between the two.
I took Juan Roman Riquelme's record as Villarreal's highest scoring midfielder.
I scored the free kick that began a comeback in an FA Cup final and ended my club's nine year wait.
I won two FA Cups with Arsenal.
kickoff: I was born on the 13th of December 1984. I played 81 times for my country, scoring 15 goals.
story: He nearly lost his leg, and he came back and played for Spain again. Cazorla had an achilles tendon that became infected, needed somewhere around eight operations, and at one point the medical advice was about walking rather than football. He had already won two European Championships and two FA Cups and been the most two-footed player in England, able to cross and shoot equally well from either side, which almost nobody can genuinely do. Two years out, then back at Villarreal, then back in the national squad, aged thirty four. Eighty one caps. One of the game's most straightforwardly loved figures.
didYouKnow: An Achilles injury in 2016 became a gangrene infection that needed eight operations and put him at risk of amputation.
Surgeons grafted skin from his left forearm, where his daughter's name was tattooed, onto his infected heel.
He returned to his boyhood club Real Oviedo on a minimal salary and helped them back to La Liga.

name: Seamus Coleman
clues: I gave one club seventeen years and climbed into their all-time top ten for appearances.
I was in the PFA 2013-14 team of the year under Roberto Martinez.
I passed Dixie Dean on my club's all-time appearance list.
I managed Everton for one match, alongside Leighton Baines.
I played right back for the Republic of Ireland at one European Championship.
kickoff: I was born on the 11th of October 1988. I played 81 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
story: Sixty thousand pounds, seventeen years, one club. Everton plucked Coleman out of Sligo Rovers on a scout's recommendation and got the bargain of a generation, a Gaelic footballer turned overlapping right-back who simply never stopped turning up. He made the PFA Team of the Year under Roberto Martinez, climbed past Dixie Dean into Everton's all-time top ten for appearances, and captained the side in the final game ever played at Goodison Park. A Neil Taylor tackle broke his leg in two places in 2017 and FIFA paid his wages while he rebuilt it. He even managed the club for a night, alongside Leighton Baines. Eighty one caps for Ireland, and not one of them handed to him.
numbers: 1 goal in 81 caps for Republic of Ireland
didYouKnow: Everton signed him from Sligo Rovers for sixty thousand pounds in January 2009.
He fractured both his tibia and fibula in a 2017 World Cup qualifier after a tackle by Neil Taylor.
He was Everton's joint interim manager alongside Leighton Baines in January 2025, winning an FA Cup tie against Peterborough.

name: Shaun Wright-Phillips
clues: I cost twenty one million pounds and scored four league goals in three years.
I have played for both Chelsea and Manchester City.
I won young player of the year four seasons running at one club.
My brother is the New York Red Bulls' all-time leading scorer.
My dad adopted me when I was three, and he is the one everybody has heard of.
kickoff: I was born on the 25th of October 1981. I played 36 times for my country, scoring 6 goals.
story: Released as a teenager, and an England international by twenty two. Wright-Phillips came through Manchester City's youth system after Nottingham Forest let him go, scored on his England debut, and was good enough that Chelsea paid a large fee for him, where he mostly sat on the bench and won a title anyway. Back at City he was better. Queens Park Rangers and New York followed, where he played alongside his own famous relative's legacy in a different league. Thirty six caps. His adoptive father is one of the most celebrated strikers in Arsenal's history, and his brother played for England too.
didYouKnow: He is the adopted son of the England striker Ian Wright, who adopted him when he was three.
He scored on his England debut, the third goal in a 3-0 win over Ukraine in 2004.
His younger brother Bradley is the all time leading scorer for the New York Red Bulls.

name: Shola Ameobi
clues: I played twenty times for England at under twenty one level and then chose Nigeria.
I scored at the Nou Camp against Barcelona.
I scored seven times against Sunderland, and only Jackie Milburn has done better for my club.
On my club's all-competitions European scoring list, only Alan Shearer is ahead of me.
I was Newcastle's first loan manager, and I still work for the club off the pitch.
kickoff: I was born on the 12th of October 1981. I played 10 times for my country, scoring 2 goals.
story: Fourteen years at one club, which for a striker who scored at his rate is almost inexplicable, and entirely admirable. Ameobi got seventy nine goals for Newcastle across nearly four hundred games and was simultaneously a cult hero and a running joke, which is the hardest balance in football to hold. He scored in the four four against Arsenal. He was born in Nigeria, raised in Newcastle, and played ten times for Nigeria late on. The exchange about what Jose Mourinho calls him, to which the answer was simply his own first name, is one of the great deadpan moments of the Premier League era.
didYouKnow: He was born in Zaria, Nigeria, and moved to Newcastle upon Tyne when he was five.
His scoring record against Sunderland led Newcastle supporters to nickname him the Mackem Slayer.
He played twenty times for England at under twenty one level before switching to Nigeria.

name: Teddy Sheringham
clues: I had never won a major trophy until I was thirty three, and then I won three in a single season.
I was the Premier League's first ever top scorer.
I am the oldest outfield player ever to appear in a Premier League match.
I played for Millwall and for West Ham, which did not make me popular in either place.
I scored the equaliser and set up the winner in a European Cup final, both in injury time.
kickoff: I was born on the 2nd of April 1966. I played 51 times for my country, scoring 11 goals.
story: He came on as a substitute in a European Cup final, scored the equaliser, and set up the winner in the next ninety seconds. Sheringham's treble season with Manchester United also included scoring in an FA Cup final, which is an absurd three weeks of work. Before that he had been Tottenham's best player for years and formed the England partnership with Alan Shearer that got them to a European Championship semi-final at home. Fifty one caps, eleven goals. He played in the Premier League until he was forty, which was a record for an outfield player, and he never looked like he was running.
honours: Football League Championship play-offs (West Ham United, 2005)
didYouKnow: He scored the equaliser and set up the winner in stoppage time of the 1999 Champions League final.
He is the oldest outfield player ever to appear in a Premier League match.
He was the top scorer in the inaugural Premier League season of 1992-93.

name: Theo Walcott
clues: I had a Nike contract at fourteen, before I had played a senior game.
My only medals are FA Cups, all of them with Arsenal.
Pep Guardiola reportedly said you would need a pistol to stop me.
I am still the youngest player ever to score a hat-trick for England, and it was my country's first competitive one in seven years.
I was picked for a World Cup squad at seventeen without ever having played a Premier League game, and I did not get on the pitch.
kickoff: I was born on the 16th of March 1989. I played 47 times for my country, scoring 8 goals.
story: Picked for a World Cup squad at seventeen without having played a single top-flight match. Walcott was Southampton's youngest ever player, cost Arsenal five million pounds as a schoolboy, and then spent twelve years at the club being both electrifying and slightly unsatisfying, which is the Arsenal condition. He scored a hat-trick for England in Croatia that remains one of the best away performances anyone has produced in that shirt, and still only got forty seven caps. Three FA Cups. Everton, then back to Southampton to finish where he started. The pace was real, and the chances it created never quite added up.
didYouKnow: He became England's youngest ever senior international at seventeen years and seventy five days.
He was picked for England's 2006 World Cup squad before he had played a single Premier League game.
He is still the youngest player ever to score a hat-trick for England.

name: Thiago Motta
clues: I won two European Cups with two different clubs.
I have played international football for two countries that have both won World Cups.
I was sent off in a Champions League semi-final for a slap that Sergio Busquets may or may not have felt.
I won eighteen trophies at Paris Saint-Germain.
I am a football manager who recently managed Juventus.
kickoff: I was born on the 28th of August 1982. I played 30 times for my country, scoring 1 goal.
story: Brazilian by birth, Italian by international career, and now better known for a clipboard. Motta came through Barcelona's academy, won a Champions League there, then injuries pushed him to Atletico Madrid and Genoa before Inter made him a holding midfielder of real distinction and he won the treble. Paris Saint-Germain gave him five league titles. He played thirty times for Italy. Then he became a coach, invented a system he described with numbers that made no sense to anybody, took Bologna into the Champions League on a fraction of the money, and discovered at a much bigger club how quickly that goodwill evaporates.
didYouKnow: He played twice for Brazil in 2003 before switching to Italy in 2011 through his Italian ancestry.
He won the Champions League with two different clubs, Barcelona in 2006 and Inter in 2010.
He won eighteen trophies in his six years at Paris Saint-Germain.

name: Thomas Gravesen
clues: A training ground scuffle broke out after I tackled Robinho.
I left Everton for Real Madrid, and nobody saw it coming.
I retired at thirty two, made my money on investments, and now live down the road from Nicolas Cage.
I represented Denmark at Euro 2000, the 2002 World Cup and Euro 2004.
I won the Scottish double with Celtic.
kickoff: I was born on the 11th of March 1976. I played 66 times for my country, scoring 5 goals.
story: One of the strangest transfers of the modern era, and nobody saw it coming. Gravesen was a combative, shaven-headed midfielder having a perfectly good time at Everton when Real Madrid rang, and off he went to the Bernabeu to play alongside the Galacticos. Fabio Capello summed him up better than anyone, saying there would be no problems with him, he was just a little bit peculiar. He won nothing in Spain. The only trophies of his career came in Scotland, a domestic double with Celtic. He never won a single individual award. He retired at thirty two, made a fortune on investments, and now lives down the road from Nicolas Cage.
didYouKnow: Real Madrid signed him from Everton in January 2005 for about two and a half million pounds.
Mike Tyson asked him for his shirt after a 2002 World Cup qualifier against Iceland.
He made his money in investments after retiring and settled in a gated Los Angeles community near Nicolas Cage.

name: Victor Valdes
clues: I won the Champions League three times.
In all three Champions League finals, I beat an English club.
My one tournament appearance for Spain was a clean sheet against Nigeria.
I have played for two great clubs, Barcelona and Middlesbrough, as well as Manchester United.
I was in goal when Barcelona beat Real Madrid six two and five nil.
kickoff: I was born on the 14th of January 1982. I played 20 times for my country, scoring 0 goals.
story: Five Zamora trophies, three Champions Leagues, and almost nobody outside Catalonia rated him. Valdes was Barcelona's goalkeeper for the entire Guardiola era, kept more clean sheets than anyone in the club's history, and was constantly described as a weakness by people who had not watched him sweep up behind that high line. Spain capped him twenty times, and he was in the squads that won a World Cup and a European Championship without playing. Then a strange, short Manchester United spell that ended in a public row with the manager, and Standard Liege and Middlesbrough after that.
didYouKnow: He won the Zamora Trophy for La Liga's best defensive record five times, four of them in a row.
He was in the Spain squads that won the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012 without playing a minute of either.
He beat Manchester United in two Champions League finals and then signed for them.
